observation.visible_scene: An outdoor scene in a dormant season: a mown grassy field in the foreground, a band of dry tan brush and a stand of bare, leafless trees filling the background under an overcast sky. A single large iridescent soap bubble (blue-green rim, yellow and magenta sheen) floats in the left-center of the frame, with a dark horizontal band across its middle that is the reflection of the distant treeline/horizon.
visible_changes: The bubble drifts slowly to the right relative to the background over the course of the clip (its center moves from left-of-center toward the middle).
The bubble's silhouette deforms: it begins as a wide, horizontally flattened oval and becomes progressively more rounded/spherical, growing taller and narrower as the clip continues.
The dark reflection band across the bubble's middle changes orientation, tilting diagonally at points and returning toward horizontal, consistent with the bubble rotating/tumbling as it floats.
The bubble stays whole and airborne throughout the excerpt; no contact, burst, or disappearance is seen.
The background trees and brush remain in essentially the same positions, indicating the apparent motion is the bubble's own movement rather than a large camera pan.
outside_clip_unknowns: How and by whom the bubble was produced, and what happened before t=0.
Whether the bubble eventually pops, lands, or drifts out of frame after t=2.67s.
The true 3D trajectory and the exact axis of the bubble's rotation, since only a 2D projection is visible.
uncertain_details: Small residual camera motion cannot be fully ruled out from the near-static background.
The apparent size change of the bubble is hard to separate cleanly from its shape deformation and any slight change in distance to the camera.
